name: Radio group
description: A set of options, all visible at once, where people pick exactly one. Use it for a small number of choices; for long lists, use a Select.
summary: Pick exactly one option from a visible set

elements.name: Options
elements.description: Two or more radio inputs sharing one name, each with its own <label>

elements.name: Hint text
elements.description: Guidance for the whole group or a line under each option

elements.name: Error message
elements.description: Says what to choose, such as "Select a delivery option"

variants.caption: Horizontal — short options in a row
With hints — a line of detail under each option

variants.caption: Tiles — each option in a bordered box

usageNotes: Use a Radio group when people must choose exactly one option and seeing every option helps them decide. Use Checkbox when several can be chosen, and a Select when the list is long.
Wrap the radios in a <fieldset> with a <legend> and give them the same name. The group is the unit; a single radio on its own means nothing.
Native radios move and select with the arrow keys, and Tab leaves the group, as in the APG Radio Group pattern. Custom versions must keep that behavior.
A chosen radio can't be cleared. Add an option such as "None" when no answer is valid, and avoid preselecting an answer when the choice matters.
A Segmented control offers the same single choice as a compact row of buttons. It suits switching views or settings; use a Radio group for questions in a form.
htmlOutline:
<fieldset>
  <legend>Delivery</legend>
  <label><input type="radio" name="delivery" value="std" checked> Standard</label>
  <label><input type="radio" name="delivery" value="exp"> Express</label>
</fieldset>
